chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdullah from Abu Ja'far from Ali ibn Hadid and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Zurara who said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said:
The prayer of the two Eids with the Imam is a sunnah, and there is no prayer before it or after it on that day until the sun passes its zenith (zuhr).

Because the meaning of this report is that this prayer is among those whose obligation is known through the Sunnah, just as many obligatory duties are known through the Sunnah; therefore, for this reason, it is attributed to the Sunnah, and we have clarified this in other places.
And it is not meant that it is a sunnah in the sense that it follows the pattern of other voluntary (nawafil) and sunnah prayers.

And whoever misses the prayer on the day of Eid, making up the prayer is not obligatory upon him, and it is permissible for him to pray two or four rak'ahs if he wishes, without intending them as a makeup (qada).
And we said this because of what we previously mentioned, that there is no makeup obligation for whoever misses the Eid prayer.
And that which indicates that it is permissible for him to pray individually is what has been narrated:

key_terms.الزَّوَال: The zenith of the sun (time of zuhr)
key_terms.صَلَاةُ الْعِيدَيْنِ: The prayer of the two Eids (Fitr and Adha)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on making up the missed Eid prayer and is it considered obligatory or voluntary?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi clarifies that the Eid prayer's designation as 'sunnah' indicates its obligation is derived from prophetic practice rather than being a purely voluntary act, distinguishing it from standard nawafil. The text further notes that no specific prayers are performed before or after it until midday, and while making up a missed Eid prayer is not obligatory, one may voluntarily pray two or four rak'ahs without the intention of qada. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly view that Eid prayer is a confirmed sunnah (sunnah mu'akkadah) with unique temporal and juristic characteristics.
